intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Germany urges Israel to allow more aid into Gaza
items.text: Germany's foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, has urged Israel to let significantly more humanitarian aid into Gaza before the rainy, stormy winter arrives. He spoke before a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels. He said the European message on aid was clear. Meanwhile, a UN official said nearly four million Syrians have returned home since the fall of the Assad government. The official added that humanitarian needs there remain acute.

gloss.urge: to ask someone strongly to do something
gloss.humanitarian aid: food, medicine and shelter sent to people in need
gloss.fall: the end of a government or ruler's power

items.title: Trump heads to Asia as Putin plans China visit
items.text: President Trump arrives in Manila on Tuesday for talks with ASEAN and the Quad, a group of the US, Australia, India and Japan. He said he may meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China during the tour, but that depends on Kim and on Xi Jinping. A Kremlin aide, Yury Ushakov, said a first three-way meeting of Putin, Trump and Xi will be the centrepiece of Putin's visit to Shenzhen on 18 and 19 November. Mr Trump said the trip is focused largely on economic issues.

gloss.tour: a trip to several places in a row
gloss.depend on: to be decided by something else
gloss.centrepiece: the most important part of an event
gloss.aide: a person who helps a leader with their work

items.title: King opens new Church of England General Synod
items.text: The King is inaugurating the new General Synod of the Church of England today at Church House in Westminster. The ceremony follows a service at Westminster Abbey. It is the first time he has opened a synod in this way. Archbishop Sarah Mullally is leading the Church. The synod has 487 members, who serve five-year terms, and its November session lasts two days. Members remain deeply divided over same-sex marriage.

gloss.inaugurate: to open or start something with a formal ceremony
gloss.synod: an official meeting of church members and leaders
gloss.session: a period of time when a group meets
gloss.serve a term: to hold a position for a fixed period

items.title: Crystal Palace name Thomas Frank as new manager
items.text: Crystal Palace have appointed Thomas Frank, 53, as their new manager on a contract that runs until June 2029. He replaces Pierre Sage, who was sacked on 12 November after only two wins in ten Premier League matches. Chairman Steve Parish said Frank is the perfect fit for the club. Separately, UEFA has backed Philippe Diallo, head of the French football federation, to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency in March.

gloss.appoint: to choose someone for a job
gloss.replace: to take the place of someone
gloss.sack: to remove someone from their job
gloss.fit: a person or thing that suits a situation well
gloss.challenge: to compete against someone for a position

items.title: Alcaraz beats Tiafoe in ATP Finals opener
items.text: Carlos Alcaraz won his opening match at the ATP Finals in Turin, beating Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2 in 69 minutes. He led 4-0 early on and saved three break points in the second set before serving out the win. Alcaraz missed four months with a wrist injury, but has won 20 of 22 matches since returning at the US Open. He has also won consecutive titles in Paris and Vienna. Tiafoe, 28, is making his debut at the event.

gloss.break point: a chance for a player to win a game against the opponent's serve
gloss.serve out: to win the final game of a match on your own serve
gloss.wrist: the joint between the hand and the arm

items.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop for you
items.text: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet, a tool that lets AI agents buy things for users. Each purchase needs separate approval with Face ID or a fingerprint. Card details stay hidden from both the agent and the seller. OpenAI built the system with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. For now, it is available only to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US, and OpenAI is rolling it out step by step. The company says the design keeps people in control of every payment their agent makes.

gloss.agent: a program that carries out tasks for a person
gloss.subscriber: a person who pays regularly for a service
gloss.roll out: to make a new product available step by step

items.title: WHO warns of 39 million deaths from resistant infections
items.text: The World Health Organization has warned that drug-resistant bacterial infections could directly cause more than 39 million deaths by 2050. The warning came during World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week. Resistance happens when bacteria change so that medicines no longer work against them. Officials have called for more careful use of antibiotics around the world. They say the problem is already making common infections harder to treat. The figures were reported through the EFE news agency, and health workers are asking governments to act now.

gloss.drug-resistant: not killed by the medicines that used to work
gloss.awareness: knowledge that something exists or is important
gloss.bacteria: very small living things that can cause disease
gloss.call for: to ask publicly for something to happen

items.title: BBC plans to move the Daily Service to local radio
items.text: The BBC is moving the Daily Service, a religious radio programme, from 9.45am on Radio 4 Extra to 5.45am on BBC local radio and online. The BBC says the local audience at that hour is broadly comparable to the current one. Canon Philip Billson, a former producer who worked at the BBC for 32 years, has prepared a motion for the General Synod. He told The Telegraph the programme would become a minority sport at that time.

gloss.motion: a formal proposal to be discussed and voted on
gloss.producer: a person who makes a programme
gloss.minority sport: something that only a small number of people follow
gloss.audience: the people who listen to or watch something

items.title: Fed survey: AI is now the top worry for finance
items.text: A new Federal Reserve survey has found that artificial intelligence is now the most-cited concern for the stability of the financial system. In total, 87% of those surveyed named AI-related risks, up from 50% in May. The European Central Bank's vice president, Boris Vujcic, gave a similar warning in Frankfurt. He said AI could magnify cyberattacks and lead to market manipulation. Other officials at the US central bank have raised the same concerns in recent weeks.

gloss.survey: a set of questions asked to many people
gloss.financial stability: a situation where banks and markets work safely
gloss.cyberattack: an attempt to damage computer systems
gloss.magnify: to make something bigger or stronger

items.title: Rockstar shares new GTA VI details before launch
items.text: Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Pre-loading opened on 10 November, and the download is up to 212 GB. Rockstar is also adding a free printable poster and a map of Leonida to the official website on launch day. After a guided demo at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, reports said hotwiring any parked car has gone. Some cars now stay locked until players get a key cloner or a slim jim.

gloss.pre-load: to download a game before its release date
gloss.hotwire: to start a car without a key by joining wires
gloss.guided demo: a short game presentation led by the developers
gloss.lock: to fasten something so it cannot be opened
gloss.launch: the day a product first goes on sale
